newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gunmen shoot at Russian car after Chechnya deal.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen shoot at Russian car after Chechnya deal.

text.p: Masked gunmen opened fire on a Russian government car in the capital of breakaway Chechnya on Sunday just hours after Russian and Chechen officials signed an important oil pipeline deal, a police official said.
Khamzat Munayev, the head of police criminal investigations, said local bodyguards in the Russian's car returned fire, but no one was injured in the morning incident.
The assailants fired six bullets at the car, which carried Vladimir Skobtsov, who works for a Russian commission set up to trace missing soldiers and prisoners of war, Munayev said.

The incident near Grozny's central Minutka Square came just hours after Russian and Chechen officials signed a deal detailing how they would repair a war-damaged oil pipeline that runs across Chechnya.

It was not clear whether there was any link between the pipeline deal and the shooting. A number of recent incidents have raised tensions after a period of relative calm and an apparent improvement in relations between Chechnya's separatist leaders and Moscow.

Nine Russian police died when their vehicle was blown up near Chechnya last Tuesday. At least three foreigners have been abducted in the area. Five Chechens were also seized on their way to Chechnya from the Caucasus region of North Ossetia.
Russia's two-year conflict with Chechnya ended last August.

The pipeline deal was one example of the improved atmosphere on a political level. It is a vital conduit for Azeri oil from Caspian Sea fields to reach world markets through Russia's Black Sea port of Novorossiisk.
In an interview Sunday, the Chechen culture minister, who participated in the talks, said an agreement signed on Friday in the Azeri capital Baku showed Chechnya was an independent country.

"We signed a three-sided agreement between the Republic of Azerbaijan, the Republic of Chechnya, and the Russian Federation, with Chechnya participating as a separate country," Akhmed Zakayev told Reuters. "That the Chechen Republic particated as a separate country again confirms our independence and the status of our government."
Chechnya has established itself as a de facto independent entity since the war but Moscow still considers it to be one of Russia's 89 regions.
Earlier Interfax news agency said the Russian Energy Ministry and Chechnya's YUNKO state oil company signed the detailed pipeline accord late on Saturday.
The agency on Saturday quoted Chechen and Russian officials as saying work would begin in the next few days to mend the 153-km (95 mile) section of pipeline, and Moscow would pay.

The deal, held up for months by bickering between the sides over the details, is intended to clear the way for crude output from an $8 billion Western consortium developing offshore Azeri Caspian Sea fields to reach world markets.

Russia and Chechnya also this weekend signed an agreement on banking which Zakayev said frees Chechnya's national bank from Moscow's Central Bank and allows it to trade hard currency and trade securities.
